subject.title: feat: add disableBoundaryAwareCache compat option for prefix-matching prompt cache providers

question: Should OpenClaw permanently expose and auto-enable `compat.disableBoundaryAwareCache` for DeepSeek, or keep the fix as an internal provider-specific message-shaping rule without a new public field?
rationale: Both directions can address the reproduced cost regression, but this PR creates an exported config/plugin API and changes the upgrade default for existing DeepSeek users; successful provider proof cannot determine that permanent product contract.

options.title: Adopt the compat contract
options.body: Accept the DeepSeek-only automatic default with explicit `false` opt-out, then require a clean rebase and refreshed checks before merge.

options.title: Use an internal DeepSeek rule
options.body: Avoid the new public field and implement the same proven message shape as an internal DeepSeek endpoint policy, with equivalent live and upgrade coverage.

recommendation.title: Adopt the compat contract
recommendation.body: Accept the DeepSeek-only automatic default with explicit `false` opt-out, then require a clean rebase and refreshed checks before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent history spans the provider cache-boundary behavior, DeepSeek compatibility handling, and exported compat type surface involved in this choice.
